question.:question/problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡3$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $3$ | $81$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3{\int }_{1}^{4}{u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot (2\sqrt{u}){|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3(\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{1}) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3(2-1) \\  & =(4)\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: positive x interval; original real logarithm branch; sqrt log>=0, denominator log nonzero in interior; q-31643 convergent improper lower endpoint
